analysis: Examined both BASE excerpts of provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/ProviderLoop.swift (533–1290) and the complete changed-range patch. The only change adds clusterUpdateDrainID and clusterUpdateDrainTask at HEAD 566–569; optional stored state alone does not establish a security regression. Surrounding BASE state includes update admission phases and the cross-process update lease (542–565), member connection/stop and pair-serving state (691–737), request cancellation tracking (606–617), and preload ownership/cleanup (760–832). Model artifact/cache bindings, memory budgeting, process X25519 generation and attestation signer selection are unchanged in this file; no observed change exposes A-001/A-003, alters T-041 cache isolation, or changes authorization or billing. Integration must examine ProviderLoop+ClusterUpdateDrain and its changed callers: how a supervisor drain is authenticated and tied to the current member connection/request, how it interacts with updatePhase/updateSession, and whether cancellation, disconnect, trust loss, aborted updates and shutdown release admission and await/cancel the drain task. These contracts affect A-018 availability and TB-002/TB-011 connection boundaries (including T-053); their implementations are outside this supplied source scope, not observed missing controls.
